title: Regional fallback wireup retrospective and action catalog
author: Sophie Kwan
body:
Summary
-------
This retrospective analyzes a cross-region outage on 2024-10-28 that exercised our regional fallback wiring (control-plane policy + data-plane routing). The incident revealed three classes of failure: (1) stale route policy cache causing incorrect target selection, (2) asymmetric model-variant compatibility leading to degraded outputs, and (3) operator tooling gaps during handoff. This doc summarizes the timeline, root causes, detection gaps, the concrete action catalog, and a prioritized experiment roadmap to prevent recurrence.

Goals of this document
- Capture what went wrong with the fallback wireup in a replicable, searchable format.
- Provide an operator-friendly action catalog with owners and deadlines.
- Propose small experiments to validate changes in staging before global rollout.

Incident timeline (high level)
1. 2024-10-28 03:12 UTC — Region-1 control-plane reached degraded scheduling: autoscaler thrash. SLOs beginning to degrade (p50 token latency +18%, p99 +42%).
2. 03:28 UTC — Smart routing policy triggered fallback to Region-2 for latency-tier tenants; policy cache TTL set to 15s.
3. 03:29 — 03:39 UTC — Several requests routed to Region-2 but landed on ModelVariant-v1a which is incompatible with the new compiler kernels (result: silent truncation and nonsense outputs).
4. 03:33 UTC — Alert: multi-tenant generation quality-regression fired; paging to Platform Ops.
5. 03:35 — 04:05 UTC — Operators attempted a manual-route flush; tooling showed conflicting versions across control-plane nodes.
6. 04:12 UTC — Partial mitigation: pinned routing policy to safe-fallback-group and disabled JIT kernel rollforward.
7. 06:00 UTC — Full recovery with follow-ups.

Detection and observability gaps
- Policy cache validation: No metric existed to correlate policy-cache-hit/miss to final routing decisions.
- Variant-compatibility health: No synthesized regression test ran at route time; compatibility matrix only verified at model onboarding.
- Operator UI: Route flush operation lacked idempotency confirmation and displayed conflicting node state (control-plane vs agent).

Root cause analysis (summary)
- Primary: Policy cache staleness. A 15s TTL plus a race with concurrent policy updates allowed a control-plane node to persist an outdated routing decision that favored a variant not present in Region-2 runtime bundle.
- Secondary: Weak model-variant compatibility constraints in the routing decision graph — model variant packaging and kernel expectations are not surfaced as a hard constraint at routing time.
- Tertiary: Operator tooling showed inconsistent state and no readonly dry-run mode for route flushes; manual attempts risked further divergence.

Impact metrics observed
- Duration: ~2.5 hours from first SLO drift to full stable mitigation.
- Quality: Regression alerts showed user-visible failure rate increase from baseline 0.03% to 1.8% for affected tenants.
- Cost: Additional token and GPU time estimated at +12% in Region-2 for the recovery window.
- Customer signal: 7 high-priority support tickets; 2 customers requested temporary capacity reservations.

Action catalog (concrete items, owners, priorities)
| id | action | owner | priority | due_date | status | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Add a routing-policy sanity metric that emits policy-candidate-hash and selected-variant-hash per decision; correlate with agent-side variant presence | Miguel Torres | High | 2025-03-15 | open | Instrumentation + dashboard + alert.
| A2 | Enforce variant-compatibility as a hard constraint in the routing graph (reject routes where target variant not present in region) | Runtime Team | High | 2025-04-01 | in_progress | Requires catalog sync API addition.
| A3 | Reduce default policy-cache TTL from 15s to 5s with adaptive backoff; add canary to 5% traffic first | Jonah Reed | Medium | 2025-02-28 | done | Canary executed in production 2025-02-12 with no regressions.
| A4 | Create a dry-run and confirmation mode for route-flush tooling; show per-node accepted version and diff | Anika Bose | High | 2025-03-01 | open | UI + CLI changes.
| A5 | Add a pre-fallback quality check: a miniature synthesis probe to verify model-variant output sanity within 250ms before traffic switch | Applied ML | Medium | 2025-05-15 | planned | Must be low-cost and deterministic.
| A6 | Post-incident customer playbook: automated customer notification + temporary credit flow when fallback causes output regressions | Customer Success | Low | 2025-04-15 | planned | Cross-team.
| A7 | Build a consumer-grade dashboard: fallback heatmap by tenant + region + variant showing counts and success-rate | Observability | Medium | 2025-04-10 | open | Tied to A1 instrumentation.

Operator playbook changes (short checklist that operators can follow during a fallback)
1. Validate active routing-policy-hash vs agent-variant-manifest (use the new metric A1).
2. If mismatch, toggle routing-policy to safe-fallback-group (pre-tested variants) via dry-run and confirm diffs.
3. If quality probes fail, abort fallback and throttle traffic; escalate to Runtime + Applied ML.
4. If manual flush is required, run flush in CLI dry-run mode, wait 10s, verify agent-state convergence, then commit.

Staging experiments and validation plan
- Experiment E1 (cache dynamics): Deploy reduced TTL (5s) in staging and exercise concurrent policy updates; measure policy-convergence time and false-positive failovers. Success criteria: convergence time < 200ms across 95% of simulated nodes and no increase in tail latency.
- Experiment E2 (compatibility gate): Introduce compatibility-check in the routing-simulator and run against the last 30 days of routing logs. Success criteria: 0 unsafe route decisions flagged when the gate is enabled.
- Experiment E3 (probe latency): Implement the 250ms synthesis probe in staging with 1k synthetic tenants. Success criteria: probe adds < 15ms p50 and detects < 0.1% regressions on known incompatible pairs.

Retrospective insights and nontechnical causes
- Cross-team communication drift: During the incident, model-onboarding owners had a rolling release; the rollout notes were not tagged in the routing-change ticket. We need a gate that ties routing policy changes to active release notes.
- Training and runbooks: Oncall operators were unsure about the route-flush confirmation semantics. We must improve runbook wording and practice in monthly gamedays.

Roadmap and next milestones (quarterly)
- Q1 2025: Complete A1, A4, and E1; update operator runbooks and run 2 gamedays.
- Q2 2025: Finish A2 and A7; roll compatibility gate to 10% traffic.
- Q3 2025: Implement A5 probe network; policy gating becomes default for new rollouts.

Owner contact matrix (who to ping for each area)
- Policy instrumentation and dashboard: Miguel Torres (Platform Observability).
- Runtime routing changes and variant gating: Runtime Team lead (An Engineering RDL).
- Operator tooling and UI: Anika Bose (Eng Developer Experience).
- Applied ML compatibility probes: Applied ML owner (Lina Park).
- Customer playbook and credits: Customer Success lead (Priya Menon).

Appendix: sample CLI commands and example logs
```
# Query the new policy decision metric (promql)
sum(rate(policy_decision_total{policy_hash!=""}[1m])) by (policy_hash, selected_variant_hash)

# Dry-run route flush (new CLI syntax)
redwoodctl routing flush --policy-id=policy-23 --dry-run --show-diff
```

Example log excerpt (sanitized):
2024-10-28T03:29:12Z control-plane-3 INFO policy_decision selected_variant=mv-v1a policy_hash=0x2f4b agent_reported_variants=[mv-v1b,mv-v1c]
2024-10-28T03:29:13Z agent-region2-12 WARN incoming_request tenant=acct-231 variant-mismatch mv-v1a not present

Follow-ups and how to use this doc
- Action owners: update the status column as items progress.
- Operators: use the short checklist in the playbook section and file a follow-up ticket for any ambiguity.
- Managers: track A1/A2/A4/A7 completion as part of platform Q1 objectives.
